text: {"status":"unresolved","evidence_ids":["ev-99f1fabd46f755abf1eb6822","ev-ed0163014611760a47c8ab9e","ev-132d01d4afe1a2815efd3eca","ev-246ad8fa7079eb079e821daa"],"request_dft":true,"proposed_test_ids":["relax-valid-pristine-and-vacancy-cells-same-signature"],"rationale":"The vacancy energy depends on which pristine reference is used, and the two available references give incompatible answers. I checked both. (1) Using the P36 pristine 3x3 total energy (ev-ed0163014611760a47c8ab9e), E_f = E(P35) - (35/36)E(P36) = -174.142 + 137.433 ≈ -36.7 eV. This is absurd. The P36 energy of -3.927 eV/atom is far from the -4.944 eV/atom of the P4 cell (ev-99f1fabd46f755abf1eb6822), and 36 × -4.944 = -178.0 eV, about 36 eV lower than the recorded -141.36 eV. That record is internally inconsistent with the other pristine and vacancy records. It is likely a mis-parsed, wrong-setup, or otherwise flawed calculation, even though it carries the same method signature and a 'reached required accuracy' marker. (2) Using the P4 unit-cell energy per atom as the reference, E_f = -174.1416 + 35 × 4.94416 ≈ -1.10 eV. This is negative and unphysical, because a vacancy in a covalent semiconductor should cost energy. It also mixes k-meshes (8x11x1 for the unit cell versus 3x4x1 for the supercell), so it is not a like-for-like difference. The vacancy cell's per-atom energy (-4.975 eV/atom) is lower than the P4 value (-4.944 eV/atom). That indicates a reference or k-point inconsistency, not a real result. A value below 2 eV would be plausible for PBE, but the numbers here cannot show it: one admissible reference gives -36.7 eV and the other gives -1.1 eV, and neither is physical. Calling the claim supported would rest on an artifact. Calling it contradicted is not justified either. The ev-246ad8fa7079eb079e821daa geometry record is also odd: 2.157 Å and 2.745 Å nearest-neighbor distances, one ionic step, only one neighbor within 2.5 Å. That suggests the pristine structure may not be a properly puckered, relaxed phosphorene. A same-signature rerun of the pristine and vacancy cells with matched k-meshes and valid relaxation could decide the claim. The scope-rebuild test is a secondary option. I would put the primary gap in the missing, consistent pristine reference, so I pick only the missing-measurement test. No peer has spoken yet, so I have nobody to support or dispute. I would challenge anyone who accepts either the -36.7 eV or the -1.1 eV number as the result."}
